summary: The root رذل (rdhl) describes something or someone as low, base, vile, or contemptible. It can refer to a person's character or circumstances, or to a thing being bad, corrupt, or abominable.
lane: رَذْلٌ ذ (T, S, M, Msb, K) and (S, K) and and (M, K) applied to a man, Low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible; (T, S, M, K;) in his aspect, and in his states, or circumstances: (T:) or, applied to a thing (M, Msb, K) of any kind, (M, K,) bad, corrupt, vile, base, abominable, or disapproved: (M, Msb, K:) fem. of the first with ة : (M, Msb:) pl. [of pauc.], of the first, أَرْذُلٌ , (Msb,) or [of the same,] أَرْذَالٌ , (T, S, M, O, and so in some copies of the K,) [or this is more probably pl. of , accord. to analogy,] and رُذُولٌ (S, M, K) and رُذَالٌ , (M, K,) which is of a rare form, (M,) [in the CK رُذّالٌ ,] and رَذْلُونَ , (T,) [which is applied only to rational beings,] and (of , TA) رُذَلَآءُ , (S, M, K,) and, of the pl. أَرْذُلٌ , (Msb, [but] said in the O to be of [the pl.] أَرْذَالٌ , TA,) أَرَاذِلُ , (T, Msb, TA, and so in some copies of the K in the place of أَرْذَالٌ ,) and [of ,] الأَرْذَلُونَ , (T, M, K,) [which is applied only to rational beings, and is said in the M and TA to be used only with the article ال prefixed to it, but is written without the ال in the K.] You say رَجُلٌ رَذْلُ الثِّيَابِ and الفِعْلِ [ A man mean, or bad, &c., in respect of clothes and of action ]. (T, TA.) And ثَوْبٌ رَذْلٌ A dirty, bad, or vile, garment; (TA;) and so ثوب : (M, TA:) or ثوب [so accord. to a copy of the T, but perhaps a mistranscription for رَذْلٌ ,] a dirty garment: and ثوب a bad, or vile, garment. (T.)

headwords.def: (T, S, M, Msb, K,) aor. رَ ُلَ, (T, S, K,) inf. n. رَ َالَةٌ (T, S, M, Msb, K) and رُ ُلَةٌ; (S, M, Msb, K;) and رَ ِلَ, aor. رَ َلَ; (Sgh, K;) He (a man) was, or became, low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible; (T, S, M, K;) in his aspect, and in his states, or circumstances: (T:) or it (a thing, M, Msb, K, of any kind, M, K) was, or became, bad, corrupt, vile, base, abominable, or disapproved. (M, Msb, K.) رَ َلَهُ, (S, M, K,) aor. رَ ُلَ, inf. n.
He had low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible, companions. (K.) As a trans. v.: see 1, in four places.

[ He reckoned him or esteemed him, or he found him to be, or he desired that he might be, low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible: or he reckoned it or esteemed it, or found it to be, or desired that it might be, bad, corrupt, vile, base, abominable, or disapproved: ] contr. of اِسْتَجَادَهُ.

(T, S, M, Msb, K) and (S, K) and and (M, K) applied to a man, Low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible; (T, S, M, K;) in his aspect, and in his states, or circumstances: (T:) or, applied to a thing (M, Msb, K) of any kind, (M, K,) bad, corrupt, vile, base, abominable, or disapproved: (M, Msb, K:) fem. of the first with ة: (M, Msb:) pl. [of pauc.], of the first, أَرْ ُلٌ, (Msb,) or [of the same,] أَرْ َالٌ, (T, S, M, O, and so in some copies of the K,) [or this is more probably pl.

: see رَ ْلٌ [of which it is both a syn. and a pl.]. Also, (S,) or, (T,) or both, (M, Msb, K,) The worse or viler, or the worst or vilest, (T,) or the bad, or vile, (S,) of anything: (T, S:) [or the refuse thereof; i. e.] a thing of which the good has been picked out, (M, Msb, K,) and the bad or vile, (M,) or the worse or viler, or worst or vilest, (Msb,) remains.
A low, base, vile, mean, contemptible, or bad, quality; contr. of فَضِيلَةٌ; (M, K:) pl. رَ َائِلُ. (TA.)

: see رَ ْلٌ, in two places. Also The worse, or worst: so in the phrase أَرْ َلُ العُمُرِ [ The worse, or worst, part of life ]. (O, K.) [In the K, immediately after the words وَأَرْ َلَ صَارَ أَصْحَابُهُ رُ َلَآءَ, we find, in some copies, وَرُ َالَى كَحُبَارَى وَأَرْ َلُ العُمُرِ أَسْوَؤْهُ; and in other copies, وَرُ َالَى كَحُبَارَى أَرْ َلُ العُمُرِ أَسْوَؤُهُ: accord. to the former reading, the meaning is, that is syn. with رُ َلَآءُ; and such SM holds to be the case: accord.
A man made, or pronounced, to be low, base, vile, mean, or contemptible: (S, * TA:) and a thing made, or pronounced, to be bad, corrupt, vile, base, abominable, or disapproved. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
